answer: We model consensus as a multi-agent game where validators post basalt staking collateral, $C$. A zero-knowledge delay bridge guarantees that the opportunity cost of identity multiplication scales quadratically. By mapping validator states via a risk atlas of subgame-perfect slashing matrices, any deviant action incurs an immediate penalty $P > C$. The expected utility of an adversary with $n$ identities is $U(n) = n(R - \delta C) - P$; for $n > 1$, $U(n) < 0$, establishing a unique, Sybil-resistant Nash equilibrium.
